transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Next: Try an ordinary evenly-distributed load to rule out load imbalance. Let me know what you find.
It's every spin now, not just big loads. It's a Zanussi, about 9 years old. Gets worse over a couple of months. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on what the drum check shows. If it's the bearings, on a 9-year-old machine that's often borderline, because the repair is labour-heavy and on many models the drum is sealed, which can mean replacing the whole tub. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings / bearing seal. Next: With the power off, rotate the drum by hand for roughness/rumble and check for up/down play (bearing) or off-centre wobble (spider). Let me know what you find.
Ok did that with the power off. It rumbles/grinds when I turn it by hand, and when I lift the edge of the drum up and down there's a noticeable clunky bit of play.
Take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it still shake or bang violently with the drum empty, or is it smooth?
It's not really shaking or banging, it's just a loud roar that gets louder as it speeds up. Noise is a little during wash too but much worse on spin.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
The checks point to the drum bearing. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's ZWF81443W, off the label on the door.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
The checks point to the drum bearing. I could not find a confirmed match for model ZWF81443W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
